[FACT] User has been getting into bird watching for about three months.  
[EVENT] User is looking to set up a bird feeder in their backyard.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in attracting a variety of birds to their backyard.  
[ASSISTANT] Recommended types of seed to attract a variety of birds, including all-purpose seed blend, wild bird seed blend, finch blend, black oil sunflower seeds, safflower seeds, nyjer seeds, and suet.  
[ASSISTANT] Suggested tips for bird feeding, including using fresh seeds, offering water, keeping the feeder clean, and being patient.  
[FACT] User has seen woodpeckers in their area.  
[PREFERENCE] User is considering getting a feeder that can hold suet.  
[ASSISTANT] Confirmed that offering suet would be a good idea to attract woodpeckers.

[PREFERENCE] User has been trying to spot a Red-headed Woodpecker but has had no luck so far.  
[ASSISTANT] Suggested ways to attract Red-headed Woodpeckers, including creating open areas, planting native plants, and providing a water source.

[PREFERENCE] User is trying to learn more about bird calls and has been listening to recordings on their phone.  
[ASSISTANT] Provided tips on improving bird call recognition skills, including starting with common birds, using multiple resources, practicing regularly, and learning in context.  
[PREFERENCE] User is focusing on the Downy Woodpecker's call, which they describe as a distinctive "pik" sound.  
[ASSISTANT] Confirmed that the Downy Woodpecker's call is a good starting point for learning bird calls and provided details about the call's characteristics.  
[ASSISTANT] Warned about common mistakes in confusing Downy Woodpecker calls with those of other woodpeckers.
